html:
Qal'at al-Bahrain is a great mound of ruins on the north coast of Bahrain, lived on from about 2300 BCE to the 1500s. It was the chief town of Dilmun, the trading land of the Gulf.

Its layers hold houses, warehouses and palaces from the time when Dilmun passed copper, timber and goods between Sumer and the Indus cities. Later layers come from the Greek, Sasanian and Islamic periods.

On top stands a fort rebuilt by the Portuguese, who held Bahrain in the 1500s. The site became a World Heritage Site in 2005 and is the centre of Bahrain's claim to a long history before oil, alongside the burial mounds to the south.
